But a lot of them are similar.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENo uncertainities founded in the above\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ee-log\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ea.ELECTROLYTE IMBALANCE:-\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; Patients with chronic renal failure, since there is an absence of renal regulatory mechanisms. In renal failure, acute or chronic, one most commonly sees patients who have a tendency to develop hypervolemia, hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, and bicarbonate deficiency (metabolic acidosis). Sodium is generally retained, but may appear normal, or hyponatremic, because of dilution from fluid retention. Following the relief of a urinary tract obstruction, hypovolemia, hyponatremia (true loss of sodium), hypokalemia, hypocalcemia, hypomagnesemia, and bicarbonate loss are most apt to occur. Electrolyte imbalances after urinary diversion vary depending on the site of urine diversion.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E*Treatment:-\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIntravenous fluids, electrolyte replacement.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA Minor electrolyte imbalance may be corrected by diet changes. For example; eating a diet rich in potassium if you have low potassium levels, or restricting your water intake if you have a low blood sodium level.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E*Most commonly cause an electrolyte imbalance are:-\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Evomiting\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ediarrhea\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Enot drinking enough fluids\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Enot eating enough\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eexcessive sweating\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ecertain medications, such as laxatives and diuretics\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eeating disorders\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eliver or kidney problems\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ecancer treatment\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Econgestive heart failure\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eb.UROSEPSIS:- is a term used to describe a type of sepsis that is caused by an infection in the urinary tract.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E*Symptoms of urosepsis include:-\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Epain near the kidneys, on the lower sides of the back\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Enausea with or without vomiting\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eextreme fatigue\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ereduced urine volume or no urine\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Etrouble breathing or rapid breathing\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Econfusion or brain fog\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eunusual anxiety levels\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Echanges in heart rate, such as palpitations or a rapid heartbeat\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eweak pulse\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ehigh fever or low body temperature\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Eprofuse sweating\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA doctor may diagnose urosepsis after confirming that the person has a UTI, which is done through a simple urine sample. If a UTI has been left untreated or the doctor thinks the infection may have spread, they may order immediate blood tests to help diagnose urosepsis.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E*Treatment:-\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIf caught early, UTIs are easy to treat with antibiotics. A person with a UTI also needs to drink plenty of fluids to help flush the urinary tract,it may not respond to antibiotics alone.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESome people will need surgery to get rid of the source of an untreated infection completely.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EQUESTION-5\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EEssay type of question.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ETreat it like ethics question and write about any case experience\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThis assignment has helped me to learn the basics of clinical practice like history taking, presentation of the case and how to approach a patient, etc ,. It would be a better experience if it was offline. till now we have learned general examination and history taking. It would be easy in learning the basics for clinical practise in offline it is quite difficult in learning all this in online.Overall I appreciate the efforts of the faculty in making General Medicine interactive and fun to learn.
